newsitem.title: HONG KONG: CITIC Pac says no asset injection talks.
newsitem.headline: CITIC Pac says no asset injection talks.

text.p: CITIC Pacific Ltd is not involved in any talks relating to asset injections by its substantial shareholder China International Trust and Investment Corp (CITIC), managing director Henry Fan said on Wednesday.
"We are not in any discussions with either CITIC Beijing or CITIC Shanghai relating to asset injections," Fan told Reuters in an interview.
The Hong Kong-based conglomerate has never engaged in any talks about assets injection with the China-based CITIC group, he added.
Fan said he wanted to dispel market rumours that CITIC Pacific's mainland parent would inject assets into the Hong Kong-listed company.
"I want to clarify this because (the rumours) misled the market," he said.

The rumours flew following local newspaper reports on Wednesday which quoted an official at CITIC's Shanghai subsidiary as saying the CITIC group wanted to give CITIC Pacific a boost as Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule on July 1.
CITIC Pacific shares surged to a record high of HK$49.80 before retreating slightly to close at HK$48.90, up HK$1.50 on turnover of HK$938.77 million.
"It's just rumours that CITIC Shanghai is coming through with some injections," said Anil Daswani, a vice president at Salomon Brothers.
Daswani said analysts were expecting CITIC Pacific to pick up new projects in China anyway after selling its 7.74 percent stake in Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd for HK$11.4 billion.
Fan said CITIC Pacific was in talks to invest in a number of new projects in China.
But he said the company had never taken any projects from its mainland parent -- which holds about 26.45 percent of CITIC Pacific -- and the possibility of doing so in future would be very limited.
"We have some new infrastructure projects (in China) under negotiation but all these projects are being discussed directly between CITIC Pacific and related provinces," Fan said.
He declined to give further details.
Analysts said the rally of CITIC Pacific shares was also because they lagged behind other red-chips in the recent sharp price rise.

Investors felt CITIC Pacific was cheap in view of its price to earnings (P/E) multipule of about 15 times, while other red chips -- Hong Kong based companies with financial support from China -- were generally trading at between 20 and 30 times.
"The latest price rise on China Light also enhanced the value of CITIC Pacific's investment in the company," one said.
CITIC Pacific bought 497.66 million new shares, or 20 percent, in China Light & Power Co Ltd at HK$32.66 per share earlier this year.
China Light shares have risen more than 30 percent from that level to close HK$0.30 higher at HK$43.10 on Wednesday.
